outcome: Fear of childbirth (as measured by the Childbirth Fear Questionnaire)
cohort: 643 pregnant women residing in English-speaking countries.
finding: Higher levels of fear of childbirth were associated with younger age, lower income, lower education, history of assisted vaginal delivery, history of episiotomy, and history of traumatic birth (both vaginal and caesarean).
mod_finding: Assisted vaginal delivery and episiotomy in a previous pregnancy were positively associated with a fear of pain, while history of traumatic vaginal birth was associated with higher scores on all aspects of fear of childbirth.
gest_age: Measured, but largely unrelated to fear of childbirth
